Assert that spell boundaries are valid

Source: R/ensure_valid_spells.R
ensure_valid_spells.Rd

Missing starts and ends before starts are violations. A missing end is an ongoing spell and passes by default; use open_end = FALSE to require closed spells. Equal boundaries are valid one-day or one-period spells. Boundaries must both be dates, both date-times, or both numeric periods. The diagnostic reason column identifies the first problem on each row: missing start, missing end, then end before start.

Usage

ensure_valid_spells(
  data,
  start,
  end,
  open_end = TRUE,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

start, end

Columns containing spell boundaries (tidy-select).

open_end

Allow missing end values. Default TRUE.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message when invalid spells are found.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged. Failures carry the offending rows.

See also

describe_spells(), ensure_no_overlap(), checkpoints.

Examples

spells <- data.frame(start = c(2020, NA, 2023), end = c(NA, 2022, 2022))
ensure_valid_spells(spells, start, end)
#> Warning: Invalid spells: start to end
#> ℹ 2 rows in 2 groups:
#>     reason           start   end
#>     <chr>            <dbl> <dbl>
#>   1 missing start       NA  2022
#>   2 end before start  2023  2022
